predecessors.note: The page says 'Delhi Sultanate'; the Sayyid dynasty is my reading for 1445.

land.text: Multan, taken by Shah Husayn Arghun in 1528

successors.note: The Langah page's infobox successor is Multan Subah (Mughal, 1530).

correction.text: Multan and the lower Doab tract round it, with Shorkot and Chiniot

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no Langah row). 'It was the dominant power of the lower Doab tract with Multan at its centre'; 'the cities of Chiniot and Shorkot' under Husayn I's successor. No area is given; the 170 km circle is my reading. The Derajat round Dera Ismail Khan was assigned to Malik Sohrab Dodai in 1469 or 1471 and is not drawn separately.

region.text: Multan, 'the dominant power of the lower Doab tract'

ledger.note: 1445: Rai Sahra of the Langahs seizes Multan. 'In 1445, Rai Sahra, chief of the Langah, attacked the city at night with the help of his tribesmen, arrested Sheikh Yousaf and proclaimed himself sultan'; the inhabitants had chosen Shaikh Yousaf Qureshi in 1438. The page names Delhi as predecessor, not which dynasty; the Sayyids ruled Delhi at the time (Cliopatria 1415-1452).

1525: the Arghuns move on Multan. The Arghun page says Shah Husayn (succeeded 1524) 'attacked Multan, capital of the Langah Sultanate, probably at Babur's insistence' and gives no year for the start; Husayn II's reign begins 1525 on the Langah page, which is the bridging year.
1528: Multan falls. 'Multan fell in 1528 after an extended siege and Shah Husayn appointed a governor of the city.'

1528: the Langah Sultanate ends at Multan. 'Multan fell in 1528 after an extended siege'; the Langah page gives 'annexed in 1527 but had autonomous authority until its merger with the Mughal Empire in 1530' and elsewhere that 'in 1541, Sher Shah Suri captured Multan, and the sultanate ended'.

wars.name: Langah-Delhi wars
wars.outcome: Shah Husayn 'successfully repulsed attempted invasion by the Delhi sultans led by Tatar Khan and Barbak Shah' and 'signed a peace treaty with Sikandar Lodi'; no land changed hands.

wars.name: Arghun conquest of Multan
wars.outcome: Shah Husayn Arghun took Multan after an extended siege in 1528; Langar Khan had assisted him.

certainty.note: No boundary is on the pages opened; the extent is a circle round Multan.

sources.title: Langah Sultanate

notes:
No Cliopatria row. Two pages (Langah Sultanate, Arghun dynasty). The Langah page is thin and internally inconsistent: the end is 'annexed in 1527' with autonomy to 1530 (infobox 1530), 'fell in 1528' (Arghun page) and 'in 1541, Sher Shah Suri captured Multan, and the sultanate ended'; the rulers table (Budha Khan as Mahmud II from 1502) conflicts with the text (Mahmud Shah I after Husayn I). This dossier ends 1528.
Not settled: the extent (a circle); the Derajat and Dera Ghazi Khan grants to Baloch chiefs (1469 or 1471); whether Multan is Sayyid or Lodi territory in 1445; Sher Shah's 1541 capture.
Counterparts needing a dossier: arghun-dynasty (Shah Beg 1520-1524 in Sindh; Shah Husayn to 1554/1556; Tarkhans to 1593; Cliopatria's Sind-Samma ends 1525 in sa-04-b).
